docs.title: What a jewel needs to match Ohm
Jewels that can roll
docs.text:
Each jewel has one affix of each kind at most: enhanced damage, minimum or maximum damage as a prefix, minimum or maximum damage as a suffix. A magic jewel has one prefix and one suffix; a rare jewel four affixes, three of a side at most. Each line is its affixes of the highest tiers, against Ohm in this weapon at their lowest and their top rolls, the best first.

Worse than OhmBetter than OhmOhmEach bar runs from the lowest to the top rolls.

docs.title: How it’s worked out
docs.text:
• Enhanced damage on the weapon raises only its base damage. The weapon’s own enhanced damage, a superior base’s and every rune and jewel in its sockets add up, and the weapon’s damage is its base damage plus that percentage of it, rounded down. Its minimum and maximum damage (affixes, sockets) are added after, so enhanced damage never raises them.
  • An ethereal weapon has 5/4 of its base’s damage, rounded down, before anything else.
  • Ohm against a jewel: Ohm adds 45% of the base damage, a jewel its own enhanced damage of it plus its flat damage. A jewel needs the flat damage that makes up the difference, which the page works out with the rounding of the weapon you entered: one point either way decides it more often than not.
  • Everything else multiplies both alike. Strength or Dexterity, skills, auras and enhanced damage on other gear raise the weapon’s damage by the same percentage with Ohm or with the jewel, and flat damage from other gear (rings, charms) is the same either way, so the difference in the weapon’s damage decides. The page compares the weapon’s damage; your whole attack differs by a little less when other gear adds flat damage.
  • A hit rolls any damage from its minimum to its maximum alike, so the average hit is halfway between. When a jewel’s minimum damage lifts the minimum to the maximum or above, the maximum becomes the minimum + 1.
  • Sockets go up to the most the base can have (at item level 41 or higher).

Inspired by HarryPe’s Physical damage calculator (its “Ohm vs jewel in Weapons” sheet).

docs.title: Run Speed Visualizer
docs.text:
Season 14 · Faster run/walk · Movement skills

How fast you run (or whirlwind) with your faster run/walk (FRW) and your skills, up to four setups side by side. FRW on gear has diminishing returns; the movement your skills give doesn’t. The chart shows what more FRW on gear would still bring.

Each setup from a standing start, its buffs just cast, at the game’s own speed and scale. The legs move as fast as the game moves them. A buff that runs out on the way (Blaze, Joust) stops counting there.

RunningWalking Distance 10 yards20 yards30 yards50 yards100 yards Speed As in gameHalf speedQuarter speed Run the race Loading the pictures…

docs.title: Setups
docs.text: Reset to the default setups Clear setups Add a setup

docs.title: Speed and FRW on gear
docs.text: Each line is a setup’s running speed (its whirlwinding speed when it has Whirlwind) as its FRW on gear goes from 0 to 300%, its skills as they are; the dot, with the setup’s letter, is where it is now. The dashed gray line is a character running with no movement skills.

docs.title: How it’s worked out
docs.text:
• FRW on gear (with Vigor’s +1% per base point: the Paladin has it whichever aura is on) adds up, then counts as 150 × FRW / (150 + FRW), rounded down: 30% counts 25, 60% counts 42, 100% counts 60, 300% counts 100.
  • Movement from skills (Increased Speed, Frenzy, Burst of Speed, Vigor’s aura, Blaze, Evade, Feral Rage, Hunger, Joust) and from a Stamina shrine (+35%) counts in full. Frenzy’s grows with its stacks (a fifth of it per stack, full at 5); Feral Rage’s is worked out from its charges, as the game does. Feral Rage is the werewolf’s and Hunger the werebear’s, so a Druid has one of them at a time.
  • Blaze gives +25% movement at level 1 and 1% more a level, up to 60%, while it lasts: 3 seconds at level 1 and 0.2 more a level, up to 10. Any class can have it from an item (Infernostride casts level 16 when you’re struck: +40% for 6 seconds). It’s one effect, so a Sorceress’s own Blaze and an item’s don’t add up: the page counts one at a time. While it lasts it leaves fire behind you as you move, and each flame burns for 2.4 seconds.
  • Charge sets its own speed when it starts: the run speed with Charge’s +150% added to the movement % from skills, shrines and slows (at least 50%, so Decrepify or a chill slows a charge too). FRW and running’s +50% don’t count, so it’s 23.44 yards a second with nothing else. In the race the Paladin charges the whole way (the strike at the end left out; when a buff runs out it charges again). Its legs play a frame of the run each game frame whatever the speed, and the two fainter copies behind it stand for Charge’s trails.
  • Whirlwind moves you at walking speed with every movement % that counts while walking (FRW on gear as above, your skills, a shrine, slows) plus Whirlwind’s own: the “Velocity” its description shows, +2% for each level after the first, up to +65% from level 34. Running’s +50% doesn’t count, so FRW and your other bonuses raise your whirlwinding speed as they raise your walking speed. With 40% FRW and Whirlwind 20 (+38%) and nothing else, that’s 10.56 yards a second whirlwinding against 11.31 running. In the race the Barbarian whirls the whole way, in the attack pose Whirlwind holds him in, with its own effect around him.
  • Speed: walking is 6 points of speed, running 9 (walking + 50%), and every 1% of movement adds 0.06 of a point. The game moves you a sixteenth of a map square per point every frame, 25 frames a second; in the yards the skill descriptions use (a map square is two thirds of a yard), a point is 25/24 of a yard a second: walking 6.25, running 9.375, and every 1% adds 0.0625. Calculators that read the points as yards a second show about 4% less. The speed never goes below a quarter of walking.
  • The race uses the game’s own pictures, facing east (screen right), where a yard is 34 of the game’s pixels across. The animation keeps pace with the speed: running plays 101/256 of a frame per game frame and walking 213/256 (the werewolf 104 and 128, the werebear 120 and 168), times the same speed % that moves you, so a faster character also moves its legs faster. Each setup starts with its buffs just cast, and a buff that runs out on the way stops counting there: Joust’s lasts 2 seconds and Blaze’s 3 to 10, the others longer than any race here.
  • Slows take off the same movement % your skills add to, in full. Cold damage chills you for −50% while it lasts. A monster’s Decrepify, Holy Freeze or Slow Movement takes what its skill level gives, and a monster’s skills are 3 levels higher in Nightmare and 7 in Hell: Duriel’s Holy Freeze is −30% in Normal, −40% in Nightmare and −46% in Hell. Map bosses, map events and ubers are in Hell. An aura-enchanted unique monster has one of 8 auras, Holy Freeze among them, at its own level divided by 7 (at most 13): from −30% at monster level 1 to 13 up to −51% at level 91 and above, in every difficulty. In the race, chill and Holy Freeze turn the runner blue and Decrepify and Slow Movement show their effects, as the game draws them. Slows add up with each other and with your buffs: chilled with Frenzy’s +58%, you keep +8%. Armor and shields don’t slow you.
  • Not shown: Blade Dance’s own movement, Teleport, and what stops you for a moment (spider webs, a map boss’s stun).

Inspired by HarryPe’s Physical damage calculator (its “FRW Calculator” sheet).

docs.text:
Nothing changes in the game: your Horadric Cube still shows Season 14 - November 20th - v2. The website gets a Feedback tab.

docs.title: November 20th
docs.text:
Season 14 - November 20th - v1 to v2. Medium value set items you haven't discovered show the Grail look, maps get a Monster Defense warning, the last map warnings come in a new order, and the IAS Calculator gets a new layout and counts skill cooldowns.

  • Medium value set items you haven't discovered get a Grail look of their own: the Grail look's four stars a side, the outermost orange, with the white dots by the name that mark Medium value, and the set Grail icon. Until now they showed their Medium value look whether you had found them or not, so a new Tancred's Hobnails looked like any other pair. Since v2 they also play the Grail drop sound instead of their own. The Minimal and Corrlorized versions draw the Grail stars with Medium value's white arrows. High value set items, and High and Medium value uniques, still look the same either way. The Unique & Set Tiers page and the Grail Planner say so.
  • +X% Monster Defense is a new map warning for characters who attack: it says how much of your chance to hit the map's monsters take away. Red when you lose 10 points or more (95% down to 85%, say), purple from 20. It goes by your level, dexterity, attack rating and +% attack rating on gear, with the attack skill bonus a typical build of your class has (the filter can't see your skill or weapon mastery), and by each map's own monsters: 14 maps' monsters are noticeably easier or harder to hit than most. Casters don't see it: a character with more faster cast rate than increased attack speed on gear (an Amazon, Assassin or Barbarian may have up to 30 more), or with a low attack rating, or with Ignore Target's Defense. T1-T3 and unique maps, corrupted too, not Treacherous maps. The suffixes that bring it (+50% to +200% on about 1 rare map in 7, up to +300% on magic ones) also bring experience and magic find.
  • Map warnings: the lines between All Resistances and the density and rarity lines come in a new order: Monster Pierce, Minions of Destruction, your Attack/Cast Speed, Damage Reduction, Monster Cast/Attack Speed, Attack Rating and Pierce, Monster Defense, Chance to Block and Physical Damage.
  • Filter Editor: in Alerts, How loud each kind of drop is counts the new Medium value Grail look and its sound with "Set items you haven't discovered".
  • IAS Calculator: skill cooldowns count. Held, Shock Web and Plague Javelin wait a second between throws, and Dragon Flight and Joust for a time that shortens with their level (Alma Negra, Leoric's Mithril Bane and Zerae's Resolve shorten Joust's). More IAS still helps: it brings the throw or strike sooner. The Damage Calculator counts them too.
  • A new layout for the IAS Calculator: on a wide screen, three columns: your setup, the answer with the breakpoints, and the attack preview, which stays in view while you scroll. On a narrower one the preview comes right under the answer. The answer's numbers sit side by side in one box, with the next breakpoints under it as rows (Next, Then, To spare). The breakpoints show your row with the two slower and five faster frame counts around it (ten in three columns); a button opens the rest.
  • Also on the IAS Calculator: the preview draws your buffs on the character as the game does: Fanaticism's flames under the feet, Frenzy's swirl, Burst of Speed (an Assassin's own or Hustle's) and the Whirlwind and Blade Dance spin, which now keeps turning from one hit to the next. The target is drawn in front of your weapon where a swing passes behind it, as in game. An attack that shoots or throws stands its target about 5 yards off, and its arrows, bolts and javelins fly at the game's speed (they flew a third too fast); Double Throw's second throw flies too. Fire Blast's and Shock Web's bombs fly in a high arc, and they and exploding arrows are drawn where they land. Fire Blast's land as close to the target as in game: their spread goes by the points you put into it, not +skills. A skill that only an item gives is listed for the classes that can use that item, and picking it puts the item in your hand (Blade Dance: Chaos in a War Fist).
  • Common builds: the builds the IAS and Damage Calculators can start from are now the most played Season 14 builds, such as Zeal with Death Cleaver, Frenzy with Doombringer and The Grandfather, Fury werewolves with Tomb Reaver and Strafe with Demon Machine, with the IAS, skill levels and auras their players commonly have.
  • Run Speed Visualizer: each setup has a copy button, so you can copy a setup, change the copy and compare the two. Clear setups starts you from one blank setup (with Undo), and the race is 30 yards by default (it was 50).
  • Monster Damage Calculator: T4 dungeons are rare only and roll only each affix's highest tier (Formidable 20-25%, Obliterating 35-45%), and a map takes at most 3 prefixes and 3 suffixes when rare, one of each when magic: past that the other affixes are greyed out.
  • The calculators share one look: the same button, list and text sizes on all five. The Damage Calculator writes minus signs and thousands separators (+1,738%), Infinity Base Comparison's chart axes keep their decimals (27.5, not 28), and Ohm vs Jewel Comparison's table and answer line up.

docs.title: November 19th
docs.text:
Season 14 - November 19th - v1. Ethereal bases to brick into rares, warnings on T4 dungeons and Treacherous maps, and a full review of the IAS Calculator.

  • Bases to brick: ethereal non-magical weapons with no sockets that your class would corrupt into a rare show with a red star after the name and the note "Corrupt this for a 50% Chance to Brick into a Rare". A Barbarian sees Mauls, Pikes, Glaives and Short Spears, a Paladin War Hammers and Flails, an Amazon her javelins, an Assassin Hatchet Hands and a Druid Great Axes, each with its exceptional and elite versions. They show on every filter level but 10 and 12, once the item level is high enough for a rare with six affixes that can roll 301-400% enhanced damage (85 to 87, depending on the base).
  • Ogre Mauls and Thunder Mauls, ethereal with no sockets, get a minimap icon and chat notification on levels 0 to 2 below character level 80.
  • T4 dungeons show the dangerous map warnings: Deadly Strike, Crushing Blow, Damage Reduction, Chance to Block, Physical Damage, Monster Cast/Attack Speed, Attack/Cast Speed, Hit Recovery, Drain Life, Max Resistances, All Resistances, Player Defense and Dual, Triple or Quad Extra Damage. They get no density or rarity lines, and no Attack Rating line: the Dungeon Scarab gives every dungeon +80% to +100%.
  • Treacherous maps show only the Deadly Strike, Crushing Blow, Damage Reduction, Chance to Block, Physical Damage, Monster Cast/Attack Speed and Quad Extra Damage warnings, now at every strength, as on other maps. Their density, rarity, bonus and "Map contains" lines are as before.
  • Map icons: a map shows a minimap icon and chat notification only where it can drop: non-magical T1-T3 maps and unique maps, outside town. Magic and rare maps and T4 dungeons, which you make yourself, no longer get one, and neither does any map in town.
  • Monster Cast/Attack Speed is one red line at every roll: purple from +70% is gone.
  • Melee Splash shows for both kinds of the Splashing affix: the stronger one, which rolls only on magic maps and is six times as common there, had no line.
  • Revealed versions: the slash between two names (Horizon's/Stormlash) is light gray instead of white.
  • Corrlorized versions: the Monster Rarity lines are back on, their number in sage.
  • Filter Editor: Features has a switch for the bases to brick, and under it you can pick your own: a tab per class, every weapon family it can use, on the filter levels you choose. Item changes can be limited to your class. The preview has a character of your own for the map lines that check yours (life, defense, block, hit recovery, resistances), set to endgame numbers you can change. In Maps, Warn and Mark write the line as the filter does (-120 Drain Life) next to the filter's own lines, density and rarity (already on every map's label) can be switched off, and a Melee Splash warning or hide works (it never matched). The preview's stat picker sorts the stats into sections, asks for a class, skill tab or skill by name, and offers each element's damage as the game writes it.
  • IAS Calculator: under the attack preview, the animation's numbers end with how they make the frames: 18 × 256 ÷ 309 = 14.91, rounded up to 15, minus 1: 14 frames. The preview shows each frame as the game does and marks a hit on the first frame that shows it.
  • Lost hits: a held Strafe or Fend can lose hits. Slowed far enough, Strafe shoots only its first arrow and Fend hits once, and Fend with a javelin loses its third hit just short of its fastest speed. The breakpoints and the Damage Calculator count only the hits that land.
  • Also on the IAS Calculator: the most IAS a weapon can carry in werewolf or werebear form counts a unique's own sockets and cube upgrades (an Ettin Axe can carry 180: Rune Master). Blade Fury follows a 20-second count in game, a blade every 7 frames with no weapon and no IAS (it said 6). Hustle's Burst of Speed counts for mercenaries. Holy Freeze from Duriel, Uber Duriel, the Corrupted Paladin and Shattered Soul slows by the right amount, here and on the Run Speed Visualizer. Fastest Frames lets you pick the attack.
  • The Grail Planner no longer says a Corrupted Ear can't go on a T4 dungeon.
  • The Monster Damage Calculator lets you corrupt a T4 dungeon too, with a dungeon's own rolls (deadly strike 15-20%).
  • The Non-magical Bases page draws the bases to brick with their star and note, and every note a base writes in its hover box under its label.

docs.title: November 17th
docs.text:
Season 14 - November 17th - v1, v2. More map warnings check your character, and the experience tag helps you decide what to corrupt.

  • -X% Defense and +X% Attack Rating check the character hovering the map: red when at least 15% more of the monsters' hits land on you, purple from 50% more.
  • Attack rating and pierce come from one affix, so they get one line: "+X% Attack Rating" where your defense makes it a warning. On the 20 maps whose monsters fire missiles that can pierce, the line says "+X% Attack Rating & Pierce" there, and "+X% Monster Pierce" (red from +30%) where only the pierce matters.
  • Drain Life checks how long your life lasts against it: red under 150 seconds, purple under 90. With no Replenish Life, a character with 600 life sees red from -41 and purple from -69, one with 1,500 life from -103 and -171.
  • Dual Extra Damage is red on corrupted maps too when its two kinds are two of fire, cold and lightning. +10% to +14% Physical Damage is red on uncorrupted maps (it was gray).
  • -X% Attack/Cast Speed goes by the map's number again (November 16th's v4 checked your character): red, purple at -20%.
  • Density: gold, red and purple are the top half, the top fifth and the top 5% of rolled rare maps, with corrupted maps' red and purple measured against corrupted maps. Low Monster Density marks the thinnest quarter of uncorrupted rare maps: density 55, 59 or 64 or less on T1, T2 or T3. Density, rarity and the lines with both have new stars.
  • The experience tag (1.72x Experience) shows on uncorrupted maps only: it tells you whether a map's rolls are worth corrupting, and once the map is corrupted the "at Level" line tells you what it gives. Gold from 1.45x, 1.50x or 1.55x on T1, T2 or T3, red from 1.65x, 1.70x or 1.75x, purple from 1.80x, 1.85x or 1.95x; every uncorrupted dungeon shows it, red from 2.65x and purple from 2.90x. Both numbers have two decimals.
  • Tiaras: unsocketed non-magical Tiaras of item level 85 and up show as non-magical Diadems do, since a rare corrupted from one rolls the same affixes. The note says a 50% chance to brick into a rare (it said 25%).
  • Filter Editor: the browser can't save into a game installed under Program Files, so the editor says so, downloads the filter instead and remembers that.
  • Corrlorized versions: Corr's fifth round: more of his gold thresholds, his potion looks, his colors on more map lines.
  • v2: the map lines come in a new order, short ones at the top of the hover box, longer ones lower and the star lines last, with shorter wordings: +X% Crafting (was Crafting Mats), X% Player Defense (was X% Defense), +X% Velocity (was Monster Velocity), Quad Extra Damage (was Quadruple) and +X% Attk.Rating/Pierce. Catalyzed is the last line, under the experience lines and next to the game's Corrupted, Treacherous and Fortified lines.

docs.title: November 16th
docs.text:
Season 14 - November 16th - v1 to v9. A map update: the highlights follow how maps really roll, and the warnings that matter most look at your own character.

  • Density and rarity have their own cuts on each tier, and corrupted maps are measured against corrupted maps. Gold, red and purple each mean something on every kind of map: before, an uncorrupted map could hardly ever get past gold.
  • Low Monster Density marks about 1 in 8 uncorrupted rare maps, the thinnest ones (it marked about 2 in 5).
  • Chance to Block, Hit Recovery and All Resistances check the character hovering the map: how many more hits land on you, how many hit recovery frames you lose, how much resistance you lose once what's over the cap has soaked the map's minus.
  • Most other map lines have new bands: small rolls no longer show, and red and purple are kept for the rolls that hurt. Unique maps count as corrupted, and get a tag line.
  • Removed: the players' +X% Attack/Cast Speed and +X% Jewelry/Charms bonuses. Ghosts, Fetishes and Hell Bovines show on uncorrupted maps only.
  • Jealousy bases: ethereal Matriarchal Javelins with 0 or 3 sockets are never hidden.
  • Corrlorized versions: Corr's fourth round of changes.
  • v2, later the same day: Hit Recovery turns red from 2 frames lost and purple from 4, on every map.
  • v3: the experience tag colors only its number gold, red or purple; the word Experience is gold, like the line under it.
  • v4: the -X% Attack/Cast Speed warning checks your character too: it shows when the map costs you a frame of cast speed (if you have at least as much FCR as IAS) or of attack speed (at least as much IAS as FCR), red for one frame and purple for two or more. Attack speed is worked out for a typical attack, as the filter can't see your weapon or skill.
  • v5: the "at Level" experience line colors its number too: red from 2.0x and purple from 2.5x. T4 dungeons, which are compared with the T3 maps, have their own: red from 10.0x and purple from 12.0x up to level 94, rising to 16.0x and 20.0x at level 98, so about 1 in 3 rare dungeons shows red or purple and 1 in 20 purple at any level.
  • v6: dungeons' "at Level" colors followed what a corrupted T3 map gets at your level: red from 9.0x and purple from 11.5x up to level 94, rising to 13.0x and 15.0x at level 98.
  • v7: dungeons can be corrupted too, so their colors now work like a T3 map's: an uncorrupted dungeon shows red or purple about as often as an uncorrupted T3 map, a corrupted one as often as a corrupted T3 map. The "at Level" line is red from 10.5x and purple from 13.0x up to level 94, rising to 14.5x and 18.0x at level 98. The Experience tag now shows on every dungeon: gold below 2.9x, red from 2.9x and purple from 3.5x (it showed from 2.3x, red from 2.6x and purple from 3.0x, which made most corrupted dungeons purple).

This update is about maps. Their highlights now follow how maps really roll, three warnings look at your own character, and the lines that rarely matter got quieter. Pick a tier and a kind of map in the bar: the charts and tables below follow it.

  • Density and rarity have their own cuts on each tier, and corrupted maps are measured against corrupted maps. Gold, red and purple each mean something on every kind of map: before, an uncorrupted map could hardly ever get past gold. See the cuts on rolled maps

docs.title: Monster density and rarity
docs.text:
Density and rarity decide how many monsters and elite packs a map has, so they get the starred lines: +84% Monster Density, +40% Monster Rarity, or +40% Rarity +84% Density when a map has both, in the higher of their two bands. The stars tell the band: gold, red or purple.

Before, one set of cuts served every map. Density lit up from +70% on T1 maps (+80% on T2, +90% on T3), turned red from +120% (+130%, +140%) and purple from +180% (+190%, +200%); rarity from 30, 60 and 80 on every tier. Uncorrupted maps almost never roll +120% density, so on them the line was always gold: a third to a half of them got it, and Low Monster Density marked most of the rest. Corrupted maps, which roll far more, used the same cuts.

Now every tier has its own cuts, from where its maps' rolls fall, and corrupted maps have their own:

  • On an uncorrupted rare map, a density line says the map is worth corrupting.
  • Rarity grows with the tier: its prefix rolls +30–40% on T1 maps, up to +40–50% on T2 and +50–60% on T3 maps, and a corruption can add more. So its cuts grow too.
  • Low Monster Density marks the thinnest fifth of uncorrupted rare maps, when they have no rarity line and no crafting materials bonus: about 1 map in 8.

docs.title: Warnings that check your character
docs.text:
Less block, slower hit recovery and lower resistances can cost one character a lot and the next nothing. A character with block or resistance to spare loses little or none of it; one who just reaches a hit recovery breakpoint loses a frame to the smallest minus. So these three lines now work out what the map costs the character hovering it, from that character's own stats, and show only when it matters: red when it hurts, purple when it hurts a lot.

The filter reads your stats when you hover the map, so each map is judged for the character you're playing. It can't see your weapon or a wereform: hit recovery uses your class's own frames. Try your numbers below; the kind of map in the bar sets the bands for corrupted maps, and how big a minus the map can roll.

−X% Chance to Block

Your chance to block is (your class's bonus + your shield's block) × (dexterity − 15) ÷ (2 × level), at most 75%. The map's minus comes off the shield's block, before that step, and the line shows how many more of the monsters' hits get through. From 30% block to 7% is 70% of the hits landing to 93%: 33% more hits.

Try: Class Level Dexterity Shield's Chance to Blockits hover box Other gear's +% blocknot on the shield The map's −X% Chance to Block−20% Before Now

Now: no line below 20% block; red from 10% more hits on uncorrupted maps and from 15% on every map; purple from 50%. Before: by the map's number, red from 10 on every map and gray below 10 on uncorrupted maps. A shield's hover box stops at 75%: if yours says 75, its real number can be higher, and the map takes less than shown here.

−X% Hit Recovery

Hit recovery works in breakpoints: what counts is how many frames a hit stuns you. The map's minus comes off your faster hit recovery, and the line shows the frames you lose: red from 2, purple from 4. One frame lost, or none, shows nothing. Below 0% faster hit recovery the frames climb fast (a Sorceress at −20% takes 31 frames to recover), and from −36% the game's hit recovery wraps around and you recover at once: that gets a gray line, on uncorrupted maps.

Try: Class Faster Hit Recoveryfrom your gear and skills, % The map's −X% Hit Recovery−20% Before Now

Now: red from 2 frames lost and purple from 4, on every map; gray on uncorrupted maps when you'd recover at once. Before: by the map's number, on uncorrupted maps only: gray below 20, red from 20. Frames count your class's normal hit recovery; a Paladin with a spear or a staff, a Druid with a one-handed swinging weapon and the wereforms have their own breakpoints.

−X% All Resistances

The map's minus comes off your fire, cold and lightning resistance, and whatever you have over the cap soaks it first. The line shows the most resistance you lose of the three: red from 5 on uncorrupted maps and from 10 on every map, purple from 15. Fully covered, it shows nothing. A corrupted map's −X% Max Resistances lowers the cap: its own line warns of that, and your resistance sits that much further over the lower cap.

Try: Over the cap+% Maximum The map's −X% All Resistances−15% The map's −X% Max Resistancescorrupted maps only Before Now

Now: red from 5 lost on uncorrupted maps and from 10 on every map, purple from 15. Before: by the map's number: gray below 10 on uncorrupted maps, purple from 10 on every map.

I picked the rolls for all 505 unique and set items. A corrupted item shows each stat once. Where a label would run past the game's 56 characters, that item drops a roll, shortens its name or joins two skill tags.
  2. Roll tags on runewords. 94 runewords show their variable rolls on a line under the name and base, with the runes' bonus included. Enigma shows its defense and its Strength and Magic Find per level; Call to Arms its three skill levels.
  3. Map experience lines. Identified maps show two lines in their description. The first says how much the map's rolls raise a full clear's experience (2.0x Experience), in gold, red or purple by how good that is for its tier. The second compares the map with an average non-magical map at your character level (2.6x at Level 98, for characters of level 80 to 98). Map Experience explains both.
  4. Boss gear tags. Identified rare and crafted gear, and magic amulets, name every boss they suit: Rathma / D.Clone / Lucion. Season 13 tagged Rathma gear only (Rathma Amulet).
  5. New versions. Minimal, Minimal - Revealed, Minimal - BIG GG and Minimal - PoE: Erazure with fewer, simpler symbols around item names, and the same filter levels, hiding, notifications and sounds (see the labels). Corrlorized - Main - PoE and Corrlorized - BIG GG - PoE: Corr's restyle, with his own colors, symbols and Path of Exile sounds. Versions has every version.
  6. Discovery Progress. The filter never hides a unique or set item you haven't discovered yet, and one in no value tier shows the Grail look until you have (orange stars). Once you have discovered every item it could be, it hides as before.
  7. New filter levels. Advanced Filtering (levels 5 to 7) sits between Stricter and Endgame. The levels that hid H5 and M5 are gone: the game's own Hide Healing Potions and Hide Mana Potions options do that now, on every level.
  8. The website. Six pages, read from the filter's own rules, show what every filter level does and how every unique, set, rare, magic and non-magical item looks.

Each pair came out closest when every Season 13 level was compared with every Season 14 level over 3,303 kinds of drops, at character levels 85 and 95.

docs.title: Season 14 content
docs.text:
The filter knows everything Season 14 adds to the game.

  • New maps: Poisoned Well (Tier 1), Dark Temple and Descent from Mount Arreat (Tier 2) have their names, tiers, resistances and map highlights. Dark Temple shows its Cursing Knights; Descent its Succubus Witches.
  • New runewords: Finesse (3-socket body armor), Deception (3-socket helms), Madness (4-socket weapons) and Jealousy (3-socket Matriarchal Javelins) appear in the runeword lists of their runes and bases, and show their roll tags. Ethereal Madness and Jealousy bases show on levels 0 to 4, and with 15% or more enhanced damage on levels 5 to 12; ethereal +3 Matriarchal Javelins with 0 or 3 sockets notify.
  • Runeword lists on runes: Rapture, Kingslayer, Innocence, Flickering Flame, Wisdom, Asylum, Destruction and Zenith are in, and the lists are re-ordered to fit the tooltip.
  • New uniques: Spectral Plate (High value on levels 0 to 7, Medium on 8 to 12) and Warriv's Warder (Minimal value).
  • 3 sockets: Splint Mail, Plate Mail, Field Plate, Ghost Armor, Serpentskin Armor, Demonhide Armor, Trellised Armor, Armet, Giant Conch and Matriarchal Javelin now hold 3 sockets. Their non-magical bases are tagged like the other 3-socket bases, and the corruption notes say C:3.
  • Stacks: runes, gems and skulls drop and stack as one item, and every gem stack shows its count (x 3). Stacks have plural names: Relics of the Ancients, Visions of Terror, Voidstones, Shadows of Hatred, Vials of Lightsong, Lilith's Mirrors, Tokens of Absolution and Pandemonium Talismans.
  • Cube recipes: the rune, gem and Jewel Fragment notes no longer ask for a key (Cube El Rune x 3 = Eld Rune).
  • Corruptions: the old Indestructible corruption now repairs durability: a gray Rep tag beside its enhanced damage. Half freeze duration (boots, gloves, belts) and curse duration on chests are tagged.
  • Jewel prefixes: the new +% elemental and magic skill damage prefixes are tagged on jewels in the Large Charm style (5%dmg in the element's color).
  • Affix levels: the best rare tier on chests, shields and Paladin shields is affix level 75 now (Guardianship, Rampaging, Immortal's, the +2 class prefixes), so the filter's 85+ rules are 75+: a rare Sacred Armor shows from item level 87.
  • Curse procs: Amplify Damage and Lower Resist proc tags show the Season 14 skill levels.
  • Guild Halls count as town.
  • Holy Water Sprinkler shows as Holy Sprinkler, so its labels fit.
  • Rejuvenation Potions stack in the stash, where their names now show on every level.

docs.title: Rare, magic and non-magical items
docs.text:
Season 14's new rare affixes made some bases worth more, so rare helms and shields are decided per base. Everything here is for unidentified drops outside town; Magic Items, Rare Items and Non-magical Bases list every base.

Rare items

  • 2-socket helms (Cap, Skull Cap, Helm, Full Helm, Bone Helm and their upgrades) show on levels 3 and 4 and hide from level 5. Season 13 hid them from level 3.
  • 3-socket helms (Mask, Great Helm, Crown, Bone Visage families, and now Armet and Giant Conch) hide only on levels 10 and 12. Season 13 hid them from level 8.
  • 3- and 4-socket shields (Large, Kite, Tower, Gothic, Spiked and Bone Shield families) show on levels 10 and 12 as their plain name with a small minimap dot. Season 13 hid them there.
  • Rare class items you can use stay shown on level 10: your own class's, a Sorceress's staves and orbs, and for every class ethereal Amazon javelins and spears and the Reflex, Ceremonial and Grand Matron Bows. From level 8, Barbarian helms hide for other classes, and so do Stag, Ashwood and Matriarchal Bows and non-ethereal Amazon javelins.
  • Level 0 notifies rare class items for your own class below character level 50, as level 1 does.

Magic items

  • Chests of any tier that can be crafted to the best affix level get the craft look on levels 0 to 4 (Season 13: elite chests only).
  • Shields that can hold 3 sockets, and Bone Shields, get that look too, and on levels 1 to 4 they stay shown at item level 94 and up (ethereal ones stay hidden on 2 to 4).
  • Amulets hide from level 7; Large Charms hide on levels 7, 9, 11 and 12, and below item level 90 on 8 and 10.

Non-magical items

  • New 3-socket bases: 3-socket Ghost, Serpentskin, Demonhide and Trellised Armor are tagged like Cuirass and Mesh Armor; 3-socket Armet and Giant Conch (Deception bases) like Spired Helm and Corona.
  • Enhanced damage, enhanced defense and resistance tags sit on a line of their own under the name (they used to sit in front of it), in the game's order, as on magic items.
  • A runeword's base line drops its Sup, Inf and enhanced damage tags, so the name and roll tags fit.
  • Non-magical weapons with high enhanced damage that no socket or level rule covered get their minimap icon.
  • Plague orbs show with their tag on every level, throwing knives follow the throwing weapon rules, Leaf staves stop being tagged where staves are hidden, Neophyte claw bases are recognized again, and Phase Blades with 3 or 5 sockets show on levels 0 to 2.
  • Gheed's gamble lines list the new uniques on their bases (Spectral Plate on Breast Plate, Warriv's Warder on Buckler).

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
Identified maps tell you what they are worth: a tag line under the name and two experience lines in the description. The November 16th update reworked the map lines since.

  • Tag line: a Tier 1 to 3 map's roll tags moved from the front of its name to a line of their own under it, 25exp 40rar 85den 120mf (experience, rarity, monster density, magic find), each colored by how good it is for the map's tier.
  • 2.0x Experience: how much the map's rolls raise a full clear's experience (density, rarity, +experience, +area level, Fortification, a guest monster), in gold, red or purple by how it ranks among rolled rare maps of its tier; no line for the weakest 10%.
  • 2.6x at Level 98: what a full clear of this map gives your character, against an average non-magical Tier 1 to 3 map at your level (Tier 4 dungeons: against Tier 3), for characters of level 80 to 98.
  • Treacherous maps (cubed with a Corrupted Ear) skip the lines that don't matter there, and their density and rarity lines show without the stars.
  • Corrupted maps no longer show the extra boss, the +% armor and weapon drop, the elemental and physical damage, Hit Recovery and Monster Pierce lines.
  • Dark Temple shows the lightning damage line (its boss casts a lightning nova), Poisoned Well the poison one.
  • Resistances follow Season 14: Throne of Insanity's magic resistance is 50, Kyovashad has new immunities (magic 105, lightning 120, fire 120), and guest monsters add theirs.
  • Tier 4 dungeons no longer list their monster resistances: their hover box already shows too much. The Dungeon Scarab, which makes them, shows them.

docs.title: Tags and descriptions
docs.text:
The tag line under the names of identified items got shorter labels, one color per tag, and the game's own stat order.

Shorter labels

  • allsk is all; replife is rep (red); drain life is drain (red, without the minus sign).
  • Magic items: 30res is 30r, 40life is 40l, 40mana is 40m, as on rares.
  • Maximum resistance is 5%max in the element's color (was 5max). Elemental skill damage on weapons and armor is %f, %l, %c or %p (was %dmg); jewels and charms keep %dmg in the element's color.
  • Mana regeneration is rgn (was regen); quiver -resistance is -25%r (was %res); jewel requirements are -15%rq (was %req); charm and jewel damage tags drop the +; javelin and bow skill tags too.
  • Damage reduction (gold), minimum and maximum damage (tan), life per kill (red) and mana per kill (blue) keep one color at every value.

New tags

  • Magic absorb abs, crit chance 10%crit, defense against missiles dvm, Decoy dcoy, Cannot Be Frozen Cbf on rares.
  • Life and mana per character level show as one total at your level.
  • The roll tags of uniques, sets and runewords add their own: defense def, open wounds ow, element skills (fsk, csk...), auras (gold), single skills (3wcry, 3smas, in tan).
  • Corruptions: Rep (repair durability), half freeze duration, curse duration. Indestructible items don't get Rep; the attack rating corruption shows only its attack rating; the demon and undead corruptions only their damage.
  • A belt or shield with the new single-element maximum resistance affix shows it in the element's color (3%max). With the all maximum resistances corruption as well, it shows 2max for all four and the element's total beside it.

Highlights

  • Rare body armor with +2 class skills gets a highlight (+2/30fcr), and the circlet, amulet, gloves, shield and armor highlights have new texts.
  • +Skill highlights (the +5 Fire Golem style description lines) use a blue and teal frame.
  • Damage reduction highlights moved up: the middle band is 8 to 17% (was 8 to 14%), the top band starts at 18% (was 15%), purple at 25% (was 24%).

Moved or trimmed

  • The sell value $ is the left-most tag of the affix line, not a prefix of the name.
  • Magic attribute tags (str, dex, vit, nrg) don't show on socketed items, where gems change those stats.
  • Corrupted magic class items don't show staffmods. A stat that gives several skills lists the highest first, as the game does.
  • Unique and set amulet and circlet faster cast rate tags are teal up to 10 and purple from 11, as on rares.
  • The All Resistances, Triple Resist and Dual Resist description lines stop at character level 80 and on filter levels 5 and up.
  • Crafted Affix Level notes: belts count from 80 (was 71), and helms get the note from 65.

docs.title: Gold, potions, gems, runes and PD2 items
docs.text:
Nothing is hidden in town any more: items dropped in town (or a Guild Hall) always show, so trades and stash clean-ups never lose an item.

  • In town, potions, keys and scrolls that the filter hides in the field show a short label instead (Stam, A, T, Keys x 5, Strangling...).
  • Potions: level 0 uses the same potion looks as the other levels (- H1 -, • H2 •, ( H4 )...). The Light and regular Healing and Mana Potions hide a few character levels later than before.
  • Gold: the higher gold hiding of Endgame Filtering also applies to Advanced Filtering (levels 5 to 12).
  • Gems: every gem stack shows its count; single flawless gems hide on levels 11 and 12 as before. Flawless Topaz now notifies like the other flawless gems.
  • Runes: stacks keep their runes' looks and sounds; BIG GG and LIL GG work with stacks; rune descriptions list the Season 14 runewords.
  • PD2 items: stacks of the boss items and of Vials, Mirrors, Tokens and Talismans show plural names with their count. Larzuk's Puzzlebox has new colors (blue, orange, yellow, tan), and high runes and the best PD2 items have a new minimap icon center.
  • The Horadric Scroll shows in town.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
These Season 13 mistakes are fixed; most were found by the new website pages, which read every rule.

  • Set drop sounds: the High value set items now play their drop sound. In Season 13 the rule checked for uniques by mistake, so set items stayed silent and Valkyrie Wing played the set sound instead.
  • Scepters: non-magical scepters with +3 Conviction or Holy Fire (0 or 4 sockets), or the Doom skills (0 or 5 sockets), were hidden unless they also had Holy Bolt and Fist of the Heavens.
  • Shop helms: maximum damage, minimum damage, life leech or mana leech each tag a shop helm again.
  • Hidden items with minimap icons: Plague orbs, Leaf staves, ethereal War Darts and some Phase Blades were hidden while their minimap icon still showed. They now show, or lose the icon.
  • Neophyte claws: no 0-socket claw was ever recognized as a Neophyte base; now Katar, Wrist Blade, Hatchet Hands, Cestus and the low claws below item level 26 are.
  • Wildspeaker and Pierre Tombale Couant were tiered on the wrong bases; they now use Lion Helm and Partizan.
  • Flawless Topaz got no minimap icon or chat notification.
  • Spiked Shield corruption notes said 2 sockets; they say 3.
  • Ral Rune's crafting note read "Ral Rune Rune".
  • Set rings with the faster cast rate corruption could show fcr twice.
  • Long labels that the game cut off (Stone Crusher's revealed name, several runeword and unique labels) now fit.
